en: Jakub, congratulations. Clearly tonight
you had a power advantage, but he's an
intelligent player and he made it
difficult for you to find a rhythm
tonight. How did you feel?
Oh, absolutely. I mean, first of all,
I'm really happy that after a very tough
physical first round that I was able to
come and I felt really good. Different
conditions compared to two days ago
playing under the lights. Even like you
said, the power was on my side. I could
feel it as well. But at the same time,
you know, the conditions were super slow
today. So it was really, really tough to
get the rhythm. It's not easy to face
these kind of conditions. And like you
said, Rinky, he's a tricky player, you
know, he's pretty fast. So it was very
tough for me to, you know, to end up the
points. But I was serving very, very
well. And I had a lot of opportunities
on the return. So I'm grateful that I
took in each set of all of them. And I
was the happier one.
Really strangely, he won 80 percent of
his points on second serve today, which
is kind of odd. On return, what was the
difficulty today?
Yeah, I mean, I mean, his first serve
percentage was pretty high. That's
probably, you know, as well, like
something that it's something that it's
not that usual. But yeah, I mean, it's
like I said, the fact that the
conditions were slower, it was very
tough for me to find the rhythm. Not
just in the ground strokes, but also on
the return.
Level of confidence, though, the way
you're playing at the moment, the way
you're building on the hard courts. How
good do you feel?
Yeah, I mean, after Wimby, you know, I
take some time off. I did really good
preparation with my team on the hard
courts. And yeah, feeling really great,
especially in Montreal here in
Cincinnati. Already played a really
couple of great matches. So I'm saying
that I must say that, of course, it's
really great to have these kind of
matches in my back before the U.S. Open.
Good job. Thank you.
